record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: For time-delay systems viewed as infinite-dimensional control systems, determine whether forward completeness is equivalent to bounded reachability sets and whether the limit property LIM is equivalent to the uniform limit property ULIM. More generally, decide whether time-delay systems admit tighter ISS characterizations than those currently available from the general infinite-dimensional ISS superposition theorem.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7.5. Although the ISS Superposition theorem (Theorem 2.7) is valid for time-delay systems, it is possible that for time-delay systems tighter results can be obtained.

In particular, it is not known whether forward completeness and boundedness of reachability sets are equivalent properties for time-delay systems (for the ODE case such a claim is true [143] and for general infinite-dimensional systems it is false [172]), and whether LIM and ULIM properties are equivalent notions, see [171] for more detailed discussions on this topic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider time-delay control systems regarded as infinite-dimensional dynamical systems. Fix a finite delay r>0 and a state space X of functions on [-r,0] (e.g. C([-r,0];R^n) or L^∞([-r,0];R^n)), and consider systems of the form
    ẋ(t) = f(x_t, u(t)),    t ≥ 0,
where x_t(θ) := x(t+θ) for θ ∈ [-r,0], u: [0,∞) → R^m is a measurable essentially bounded input, and f satisfies standard regularity assumptions ensuring local existence and uniqueness of solutions.

Define the following properties:
  (FC) Forward completeness: for every initial state x_0 ∈ X and every admissible input u, the solution exists for all t ≥ 0.
  (BRS) Bounded reachability sets: for every T > 0 and every R > 0, the set {x_t : t ∈ [0,T], ‖x_0‖_X ≤ R, ‖u‖_∞ ≤ R} is bounded in X.
  (LIM) Limit property: there exists γ ∈ K_∞ such that for every x_0 ∈ X and every input u, liminf_{t→∞} ‖x(t)‖ ≤ γ(‖u‖_∞).
  (ULIM) Uniform limit property: there exists γ ∈ K_∞ such that for every ε > 0 and every R > 0 there is τ = τ(ε,R) with the property that for every ‖x_0‖_X ≤ R and every input u, there exists t ≤ τ with ‖x(t)‖ ≤ γ(‖u‖_∞) + ε.

Questions:
(a) For time-delay systems on a given state space X, is (FC) equivalent to (BRS)?
(b) For time-delay systems, is (LIM) equivalent to (ULIM)?
(c) More generally, do time-delay systems admit strictly tighter input-to-state stability (ISS) characterizations than those provided by the general infinite-dimensional ISS superposition theorem?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent research has partially resolved part (a). On the state space C([-r,0];R^n) of continuous functions, forward completeness has been shown NOT to imply boundedness of reachability sets, with explicit counterexamples (Chaillet, Pepe, Mironchenko, Wirth, 2023). On the state space L^∞([-r,0];R^n) of essentially bounded measurable functions, forward completeness DOES imply bounded reachability sets (Mironchenko, Chaillet, Pepe, Wirth, 2024, IEEE TAC). Parts (b) and (c) regarding LIM vs ULIM equivalence and the existence of tighter ISS characterizations for time-delay systems beyond the general superposition theorem remain, to our knowledge, open.

status_evidence.title: Forward completeness does not imply bounded reachability sets ... for time-delay systems
status_evidence.snippet: An example of a time-invariant time-delay system that is forward complete but whose reachability sets from bounded initial conditions are not bounded over compact time intervals.
status_evidence.claim: FC is not equivalent to BRS in general for time-delay systems on C([-r,0]).

status_evidence.title: Forward completeness implies bounded reachable sets for time-delay systems on L^∞
status_evidence.snippet: Forward completeness implies the bounded reachability sets property in the state space of essentially bounded measurable functions.
status_evidence.claim: FC implies BRS on the state space L^∞([-r,0];R^n), partially settling (a).
